common_name: Titan's Glory Bearded Iris (Dykes Medal Deep Violet-Blue Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil; Titan's Glory won the American Iris Society's Dykes Medal for its huge, richly colored blooms and vigorous growth.

directions: Set rhizomes horizontally with the top surface exposed to the sun, never buried, in well-drained soil in full sun; soggy conditions invite rhizome rot far more readily than this iris is bothered by drought. Titan's Glory earned the American Iris Society's Dykes Medal for its exceptionally large, deep violet-blue flowers with excellent form and substance, held on tall, sturdy, well-branched stems that carry an unusually high bud count for a long bloom season. Its vigorous growth and heavy increase have made it a widely grown garden and exhibition standard for decades. Divide congested clumps every three to four years after bloom, discarding the older woody center and replanting healthy outer fans; good drainage is essential to prevent rhizome rot.

Its subtle color makes it a versatile companion for both cooler blues and violets and warmer pastel plantings. Bred by Schreiner's Iris Gardens, it has remained a garden and exhibition standard for its dependable, vigorous performance and clean, saturated blue color. planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil; Conjuration won the American Iris Society's Dykes Medal for its unusual blended blue-violet coloring and strong branching.

Conjuration earned the American Iris Society's Dykes Medal for its distinctive blended flowers combining soft blue and violet tones with excellent ruffling and substance, held on tall, well-branched stems with a generous bud count that extends the bloom season. Its subtly shifting color reads differently depending on the light, giving the flowers extra depth compared to solid-colored iris cultivars.
